### What does this PR do? Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group. Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph OLD["Current upstream"] direction LR A["Probe a free port"] --> B["Close probe socket
Publish port"] B --> C["Worker startup
Port is unbound"] C --> D["Rank 0 binds TCPStore
May fail: EADDRINUSE"] end subgraph NEW["This PR"] direction LR E["Start rank 0
Bind and retain TCPStore"] --> F["Publish bound endpoint"] F --> G["Initialize process groups
Rank 0 reuses listener
Peers connect to it"] end OLD ~~~ NEW classDef risk fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d classDef bound fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d class C risk class E,F,G bound ``` Related issues: [verl-omni#759](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/issues/759) and [verl#3147](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/3147). Related PR [#5706](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/5706) addresses the same startup race with a temporary reservation socket released before the first worker RPC. This implementation instead retains the TCPStore listener itself, avoiding the socket-to-server handoff and supporting process-group initialization inside worker constructors. ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: [port](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+port+in%3Atitle), [TCPStore](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+TCPStore+in%3Atitle%2Cbody), [EADDRINUSE](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+EADDRINUSE+in%3Atitle%2Cbody), [rendezvous](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+rendezvous+in%3Atitle%2Cbody). - [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI) - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off` - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]` - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test` - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title. - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching` ### Test The following regression tests ran on `0d81922ee56e` (the final commit) from the repository root. | Item | Version | |---|---| | Hardware | 1 host, 4 × NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB | | Python | 3.12.15 | | PyTorch | 2.13.0+cu130 | | Ray | 2.58.0 | ```bash # Full pre-commit: passed; no source changes. python -m pre_commit install python -m pre_commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always # CPU regressions: 11 passed. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest \ tests/single_controller/test_ray_local_envs_on_cpu.py \ tests/single_controller/test_fused_workers_on_cpu.py \ tests/single_controller/test_decorator_on_cpu.py \ tests/single_controller/test_auto_padding_on_cpu.py \ -q --tb=short # Existing GPU regressions: 8 passed across these four commands. python -m pytest tests/single_controller/test_worker_group_torch.py -q --tb=short # 2 passed python -m pytest tests/single_controller/test_split_resource_pool.py -q --tb=short # 4 passed python -m pytest tests/single_controller/test_colocated_workers.py -q --tb=short # 1 passed python -m pytest tests/single_controller/test_colocated_workers_fused.py -q --tb=short # 1 passed ``` ### API and Usage Example This PR changes internal master-port allocation and binding during worker startup. No changes to user code or configuration are required. ### Design & Code Changes - Wrap rank zero to bind a `multi_tenant=True` TCPStore before entering the original constructor, retaining the listener for the actor's lifetime. ### What does this PR do? Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group. Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph OLD["Current upstream"] direction LR A["Probe a free port"] --> B["Close probe socket
Publish port"] B --> C["Worker startup
Port is unbound"] C --> D["Rank 0 binds TCPStore
May fail: EADDRINUSE"] end subgraph NEW["This PR"] direction LR E["Start rank 0
Bind and retain TCPStore"] --> F["Publish bound endpoint"] F --> G["Initialize process groups
Rank 0 reuses listener
Peers connect to it"] end OLD ~~~ NEW classDef risk fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d classDef bound fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d class C risk class E,F,G bound ``` Related issues: [verl-omni#759](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/issues/759) and [verl#3147](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/3147).
